sources.title: David L. DeMets and K. K. Gordon Lan, Interim Analysis: The Alpha Spending Function Approach, Statistics in Medicine 13 (1994)
sources.locator: PDF pp. 2–3 (group-sequential boundary procedure and null crossing probabilities) and pp. 6–7 (information fractions, alpha-spending equation, Pocock and O’Brien–Fleming-type functions, and covariance discussion). Complete article text was retrieved; only these focused pages support this pair.

Classical constant or square-root critical-value sequences
contents.reason: These fixed-boundary families are not asserted as outputs here; the assigned page instead recalibrates the named spending curves under the stipulated joint law.

contents.name: Estimated information fractions and non-independent or asymptotic increment models
contents.reason: The theorem assumes prescheduled information fractions and an exact canonical Gaussian null law, and makes no extension to estimated timing or an asymptotic covariance approximation.

sources.title: Michael J. Grayling, James M. S. Wason, and Adrian P. Mander, Group Sequential Clinical Trial Designs for Normally Distributed Outcome Variables, The Stata Journal 18(2) (2018)
sources.locator: PDF pp. 2–4: the known-variance normal model and standardized statistics, the canonical joint mean/covariance law, two-sided stopping rules, and joint-normal operating-characteristic calculation.

contents.name: Known-variance two-treatment sampling model and standardized cumulative statistic
contents.reason: This page takes the canonical Gaussian null vector as a model assumption and does not prove that a particular trial data-generating process yields it.

contents.name: Canonical joint distribution with information-fraction covariance
Two-sided stopping rule and decomposition into crossing events
Joint-normal operating-characteristic integration for calibrated boundaries
Type-II error targets, treatment-effect alternatives, and sample-size optimization
contents.reason: The assigned theorem proves only exact simple-null cumulative type-I spending; it makes no power, type-II, treatment-effect, or sample-size claim.

sources.locator: §§5.3–5.3.1, printed pp. 72–73 / PDF pp. 93–94: group-sequential testing, the linear-combination z/t and multivariate global statistics, and the need to derive stagewise critical values from the joint distribution.
